hook: Drained bogs and swamps cause 3% of human-made climate warming.

sections.voiceover: Drained bogs and swamps cause 3% of human-made climate warming.
sections.visual_cue: Aerial footage of cracked, dried peatland soil stretching toward the horizon under hazy sunlight.
b_roll: cracked dried peat soil aerial view

sections.voiceover: Over 220 years, humans drained peatlands for farming and land development. How did dried soil release 600 billion tons of carbon?
sections.visual_cue: Historical archive style footage of drainage canals cut through peat bogs, transitioning to soil testing equipment.
sections.sfx_cue: Subtle earth digging sound followed by wind whistling over barren ground
b_roll: soil moisture research equipment field work

sections.voiceover: However, a Nature study shows that decomposition accelerates rapidly as water drains from these bogs.
sections.visual_cue: Extreme macro close-up of decaying organic peat fibers exposed to ambient air oxygen.
b_roll: peat moss texture macro exposure to oxygen

sections.voiceover: MIT researcher Jevan B. Yu led the team quantifying this 2.7 percent warming impact. These bogs store more carbon than all living vegetation combined.
sections.visual_cue: High-contrast map visualization showing global peatland distribution and relative carbon density comparison against global forest biomass.
b_roll: lush tropical forest canopy aerial shot

sections.voiceover: Draining peatlands created a long-term legacy of 3% global warming.
sections.visual_cue: Wide landscape shot of a protected natural wetland fen glowing under golden hour light.
b_roll: natural protected wetland fen golden hour light
